detail: Vida's audit (scene 10) badges all 5 MUAC photos 'Hyperzoomed' with high AI confidence (0.88-0.93) and the scene claims the badge marks photos 'where the child's arm is not visible'. Inspecting the images, only ~2 of 5 are literally hyperzoomed (tape window fills the frame, no arm/context); the other ~3 show finger obstruction, backlight glare, or tape mispositioning where the arm IS partly visible. The uniform 'Hyperzoomed' label overclaims a single AI defect category across images that show varied defects, so 'verify the machine's finding against the images' does not literally hold for 3/5 photos. The overall story (AI caught misleading photos -> all fail -> suspension) is true and the human review note 'framing makes the reading impossible to verify' is accurate.
fix_recommendation: Align the AI badge to the image content by one of: (a) re-seed Vida's audit with a bounded 2-photo pure-hyperzoom corpus so every 'Hyperzoomed' badge matches its image; (b) relabel the 3 non-hyperzoom photos with their true AI defect category (tape-usage / equipment / misleading); or (c) soften the scene-10 narration and concept_claim to 'framing-flagged' rather than the specific 'Hyperzoomed'. Advisory / non-blocking; operator pre-scoped option (a).
